issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String (SealSaloon(String)), but both the template (Main.java) and the provided solution implement and use a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon()). This mismatch will confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether they must store a saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the template and solution to provide a constructor that matches the spec: public SealSaloon(String name) (and adjust calls in Main to use new SealSaloon("SomeName")), and optionally store the name in a field; or (B) revise the problem statement and UML to accept a no-argument constructor if a saloon name is not required. Prefer option A to follow the UML/spec as written.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for SealSaloon: the problem statement and UML specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) (a saloon name parameter), but both the provided template usage (Main) and the reference solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This inconsistency can confuse students about which constructor they must implement and how to initialize the saloon.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and template to provide a constructor matching the problem statement (public SealSaloon(String name)) and initialize any needed fields, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to expect a no-argument constructor (public SealSaloon()). Prefer (A) if the saloon name is intended to be part of the exercise; otherwise choose (B) and adjust the UML and description accordingly.
